text:
[LGRA.3.1] File-level productions:

```
file ::= use_decl? (import_decl | top_level_decl)*

use_decl ::= 'use' NAME NEWLINE
          |  'use' NAME ':' NEWLINE INDENT setting_line+ DEDENT

setting_line ::= NAME ':' BOOL_LIT NEWLINE

top_level_decl ::= const_decl        # [LGRA.4]
                |  schema_decl       # [LGRA.5]
                |  rule_decl         # [LGRA.6]
                |  series_decl       # [LGRA.7]
                |  service_decl      # [LGRA.23]
                |  unit_decl         # [LUNI.4]
                |  opaque_decl       # [LOPQ.2.1]
                |  test_decl         # [LGRA.21.1]
                |  initial_block     # [LGRA.24.1]
```

`import_decl` is [LIMP.2.1.1]'s two import forms. Each `top_level_decl`
alternative is defined at the clause beside it.

**Residue the grammar does not carry ([STYL.2.15.4]):** every `import_decl`
precedes every `top_level_decl` — an import after one is a compile error, not a
parse error ([LIMP.2.3.2]); whether a file may or must have a `use_decl`
([LDIA.2.10.1]); that each `setting_line` names a registered capability
([LDIA.3.3.2]) at most once ([LDIA.3.3.6]); and how the block resolves
against the named dialect ([LDIA.3.3.1]).

(Comments and blank lines are stripped at the lexer level
per LGRA.2.4 / LGRA.2.2.3 and never reach the parser.)
